robotbuild_meta_desc: Build your own Bruut field robot: hole-grid frame, wheel units with hub motor, steering heads with stepper motor. With FreeCAD model, drawings and four versions.
robotbuild_hero_subtitle: A frame of box-section beams with a hole pattern, four wheel units and standard electronics. All drawings and models are open on GitHub.
robotbuild_prototype_alt: A team member next to the Bruut prototype with a seat in a grass field
robotbuild_workshop_desc: Everything on this page has really been built and driven. The electronics are deliberately still visible, so everything can be rebuilt, re-measured or rewired between two test drives.
robotbuild_photo_1: The frame on four wheel units, from the front
robotbuild_photo_2: Steering head with stepper motor above the front wheel
robotbuild_photo_3: Side view: box beams on the wheel brackets
robotbuild_photo_4: From above: the hole pattern in the box beams
robotbuild_photo_5: Both steering heads, with the GNSS antenna between them
robotbuild_cad_desc: The model is rebuilt from the OpenSCAD files and the photos of the prototype. Every dimension lives in one parameter file: change it and the whole model is rebuilt.
robotbuild_steer_desc: Each front wheel turns on its own steering shaft with a NEMA 34 and a 5:1 planetary gearbox. The inner wheel steers sharper than the outer: at 25° centre angle 29.5° against 21.6°.
robotbuild_frame_desc: Box beams with a continuous hole pattern. You set track width and wheelbase by bolting the beams into a different row of holes, without welding.
robotbuild_wheelunit_desc: One hub motor, two side plates and a top plate with slotted holes. The unit bolts to the frame as one module: swapping a motor takes minutes.
robotbuild_steerhead_desc: Two flange bearings in plates below and above the frame, a Ø 25 mm steering shaft and the stepper motor on top.
robotbuild_maintenance_desc: 60 V maximum, a main switch and a clearly visible emergency stop. Removable power tool battery packs and electronics in accessible boxes.
robotbuild_laser_label: Laser cutting for all four wheel modules, incl. VAT
robotbuild_laser_desc: 8 side plates, 8 axle brackets and 4 top plates. All drawings are in the repository, so any sheet metal shop can make them.
robotbuild_versions_desc: The Agbot XL has 16-inch hub motors, 200/70R16 tyres and 60 mm box beams. The same software, a different size.
robotbuild_compare_side: Side view at the same scale, with a 1.80 m person.
robotbuild_compare_top: Top view, grid lines every 500 mm.
robotbuild_compare_video: Both robots drive the same turn. The XL has a 40% larger turning radius.
robotbuild_progress_desc: This is where the project stands today. Every step, including the ones that went wrong, is on the YouTube channel.
robotbuild_steering_desc: The robot started as a differential-drive two-wheeler, but accurate line following was hard to tune. Now it steers like a tricycle with a pure pursuit algorithm that keeps it on its path.
robotbuild_ardupilot_desc: For RTK and autonomous driving we build on ArduPilot. The robot drives missions between AB points on its own; line following does not yet work on every surface and in every turn.
robotbuild_vision_desc: A global shutter camera gives no skewed images while driving. With SAHI (sliced inference) small objects such as young plants are recognised noticeably better.
robotbuild_steppers_desc: Implements need to move sideways and up and down. NEMA 34 stepper motors have enough torque for a side-shift frame and are easy to control.
robotbuild_spot_spraying_desc: Spot spraying builds on the open-source Open Weed Locator (OWL). Innovators like Guy Coleman show the open-source community at its best.
robotbuild_inrow_desc: Computer vision decides which plant stays. There are working tests for hoeing between cauliflower, side-shift hoeing and recognising spindle trees in the row.
robotbuild_videos_cta_desc: Every build step, test drive and setback is filmed and explained. A new video appears on the channel every few weeks.
robotbuild_play_video: Play the video: the robot in action
